findings.title: Generic fused LoRA QKV wrapper applies RoPE on Cohere2's NoPE (full-attention) layers
findings.claim: Cohere2 alternates sliding-window layers (RoPE) with full-attention layers that are deliberately NoPE: transformers 5.15 modeling_cohere2.py:229 guards the rotary call with `if self.sliding_window is not None:`. The generic fused wrapper `_make_fused_qkv_attention_forward` applies `apply_rotary_pos_emb` unconditionally (qkv.py:131-133), so every 4th Cohere2 layer silently gets rotary embeddings that upstream never applies. Cohere2Attention is routed to this generic wrapper by `_resolve_fused_qkv_forward_factory` (qkv.py:44-45). Fusion is enabled by default (`apply_model_patches(..., peft=True)`), so a Cohere2 + LoRA DP fine-tune on CUDA trains a different model than the one it loaded, with no warning.
findings.failure_scenario: Load c4ai-command-r7b (Cohere2, layer_types = 3x sliding_attention + 1x full_attention repeating), wrap with LoraConfig(target_modules=['q_proj','k_proj','v_proj']), call opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(model), train on CUDA. Layers 3, 7, 11, ... compute attention with RoPE-rotated Q/K although the architecture defines them as NoPE. Forward, loss and per-sample gradients are all wrong for 25% of the layers; nothing raises.
evidence: CURRENT TREE packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/components/qkv.py:19-28 — `_FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES = {... "Cohere2Attention", ...}`; qkv.py:127-133 — `apply_rotary_pos_emb = model_module.apply_rotary_pos_emb; cos, sin = position_embeddings; query_states, key_states = apply_rotary_pos_emb(query_states, key_states, cos, sin)` with no `sliding_window` guard.

UPSTREAM .venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/transformers/models/cohere2/modeling_cohere2.py:228-230 — `cos, sin = position_embeddings` / `if self.sliding_window is not None:` / `    query_states, key_states = apply_rotary_pos_emb(...)`; line 198 — `self.sliding_window = config.sliding_window if config.layer_types[layer_idx] == "sliding_attention" else None`.

RUN (CPU, `torch.Tensor.is_cuda` monkeypatched True to force the fused branch; script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/qkvaudit/cohere2_layer.py): tiny Cohere2 with layer_types ['sliding_attention','full_attention'], per-layer self_attn output, unfused vs fused — `layer 0 sliding_window=4 maxdiff=0.000000e+00 rel=0.000%` / `layer 1 sliding_window=None maxdiff=7.657375e-03 rel=6.067%`. Only the NoPE layer diverges, which isolates the cause to the unconditional rotary call.
Whole-model run (cohere2_rope.py): `fused attn modules: 2`, `max abs diff: 0.00010981` on logits, `allclose: False`.

The only Cohere2 fused-LoRA test, packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_fused_lora_parallel_residual.py:47-53 and :127, builds `Cohere2Config(num_hidden_layers=1, ...)`. Verified with `.venv/bin/python -c "...Cohere2Config(num_hidden_layers=1...).layer_types"` -> `['sliding_attention']`: the test never instantiates a full-attention layer, and it compares vmap vs eager of the *same fused* model, never against the unfused upstream path.

Commit context: Cohere2Attention was already in the generic set before the delta; the four delta commits 41722a0b (#947), 414504dc (#949), 8ced13cf (#951), bf2190b9 (#950) added Qwen2/GLM4/Gemma3/Qwen3 and built dedicated wrappers for the two families whose pipeline differs, but left Cohere2 on the generic wrapper.
findings.fix_sketch: Either give Cohere2 a dedicated wrapper (as Gemma3/Qwen3 got) that reproduces `if self.sliding_window is not None: apply_rotary_pos_emb(...)`, or make the generic wrapper conditional on the same predicate. Safest immediate action: remove "Cohere2Attention" from `_FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES` until a faithful wrapper exists. Add a device-independent pipeline test in the style of `_install_reference_fused_qkv` (tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:126-139) that compares the generic wrapper against upstream `attn(...)` for a Cohere2 config with num_hidden_layers >= 4.

findings.title: Generic fused LoRA QKV wrapper drops sliding_window and softcap, silently disabling Mistral/Gemma2 windowed attention and Gemma2 logit softcapping
findings.claim: The generic wrapper calls `attention_interface(self, q, k, v, attention_mask, dropout=..., scaling=self.scaling, **kwargs)` and never forwards the family-specific arguments that upstream passes: `sliding_window` (Mistral, Qwen2, Gemma2, Cohere2) and `softcap=self.attn_logit_softcapping` (Gemma2). Opaque's own Mistral/Ministral/Gemma2 family patches install `apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch`, whose `vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask` deliberately returns `None` for a no-padding SDPA prefill and delegates the look-back limit to the attention implementation via the `sliding_window` kwarg (runtime/masking.py:110-144). Because the fused wrapper drops that kwarg, the window is applied by neither the mask nor the kernel: the model silently becomes full-causal. Gemma2's `vmap_eager_attention_forward_gemma2` / `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2` likewise default `softcap=None`, so `attn_logit_softcapping` is silently disabled. The dedicated Gemma3 and Qwen3 wrappers added in this delta *do* pass `sliding_window` (qkv_gemma3.py:83, qkv_qwen3.py:81) — the generic wrapper they were factored out of was never fixed.
findings.failure_scenario: Mistral-7B-v0.1 (config.sliding_window=4096), LoRA on q/k/v, `attn_implementation='sdpa'`, no padding mask, sequence length > 4096, `opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(model)` on CUDA. `create_sliding_window_causal_mask` returns None (compact path), the fused wrapper omits `sliding_window`, `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window` falls through to plain causal SDPA, and every query attends to the whole prefix. Training silently optimizes a different architecture. Separately, any Gemma2 + LoRA run loses attention-logit softcapping at all sequence lengths.
evidence: CURRENT TREE qkv.py:155-164 — the attention_interface call passes only `attention_mask`, `dropout`, `scaling`, `**kwargs`.

UPSTREAM transformers/models/mistral/modeling_mistral.py:172 `sliding_window=getattr(self.config, "sliding_window", None),  # main diff with Llama`; models/qwen2/modeling_qwen2.py:228 `sliding_window=self.sliding_window,  # main diff with Llama`; models/gemma2/modeling_gemma2.py:281-282 `sliding_window=self.sliding_window,` + `softcap=self.attn_logit_softcapping,`.

CURRENT TREE packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/models/mistral.py:32-33 installs `sdpa_attention_replacement=vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window` and `masking_module_patcher=apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch`; runtime/masking.py:132-143 returns `None` (no mask) when `_can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window(...)`; components/attention.py:277-312 `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window` only applies the band `if ... sliding_window is not None ...`, otherwise delegates to plain `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward`.

The fused output is *bit-identical* to the same model with `sliding_window=None` — the window is entirely gone; the unfused opaque path is bit-exact with upstream.

So the Qwen2 addition in 41722a0b (#947) is latent rather than live — but it inherits the same defect for `flash_attention_*`, where `_backend_enforces_sliding_window` (runtime/masking.py:42-48) deliberately leaves the window out of the mask.

docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:25-28 calls the fused kernels "Drop-in, numerically equivalent replacements" and :349-353 lists "Mistral, Gemma, Gemma2, Granite, Cohere2, Qwen2 (generic wrapper)" as eligible while noting only the dedicated wrappers keep "Gemma3's sliding-window argument — intact".
findings.fix_sketch: Make the generic wrapper forward the same arguments the family's own forward does. Minimal version: `extra = {}` then `if getattr(self, 'sliding_window', None) is not None or hasattr(self.config, 'sliding_window'): extra['sliding_window'] = getattr(self, 'sliding_window', getattr(self.config, 'sliding_window', None))` and `if getattr(self, 'attn_logit_softcapping', None) is not None: extra['softcap'] = self.attn_logit_softcapping`, passed into the attention_interface call. Better: replace name-set routing with a per-family wrapper table so that adding a family forces an explicit decision about its extra kwargs, and add a device-independent parity test per eligible family (the `_install_reference_fused_qkv` pattern already used for Gemma3).

findings.title: Fused QKV never got the fp32-adapter fallback that #977 added to the LoRA Linear and MLP paths
findings.claim: Commit 5b41925c 'fix(patches): preserve fused LoRA mixed-precision behavior (#977)' introduced `_active_adapters_use_dtype` / `_lora_projections_use_dtype` (components/_utils.py:20-37) and wired them into `linear.py:52-55` and `mlp.py:58-62`: when CUDA autocast is off and the active adapters are not already in the hidden-state dtype, the fused kernel is bypassed and PEFT's own forward runs so the adapter branch keeps its fp32 precision. `_opaque_fused_lora_qkv` in qkv.py has no such guard — it unconditionally does `hidden_states.to(_active_lora_dtype(hidden_states))` and `Opaque_LoRA_QKV.forward` then casts the fp32 adapters down via `cast_to_dtype(active_cuda_dtype(X), ...)` (kernels/lora.py:511-513). The result is an inconsistency inside one attention block: o_proj and the MLP honour the fp32 adapters, q/k/v do not.
findings.failure_scenario: The standard bf16-weights + fp32-adapters PEFT setup (`model.to(torch.bfloat16)` then `get_peft_model(...)`, which keeps lora_A/lora_B in fp32 by default) run without `torch.autocast`. o_proj falls back to PEFT and computes `base + fp32_delta` with a single rounding; q/k/v run fused and compute the whole adapter delta in bf16. Per-sample gradients on the DP path are then produced from a lower-precision forward for q/k/v only, and the model does not match the PEFT reference the tests in #977 were written to defend.
evidence: CURRENT TREE packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/components/linear.py:52-55 — `if not torch.is_autocast_enabled("cuda") and not _active_adapters_use_dtype(self, target_dtype): return original(self, x, *args, **kwargs)`; mlp.py:58-62 — same guard via `_lora_projections_use_dtype(self, ("gate_proj","up_proj","down_proj"), dtype)`.

CURRENT TREE qkv.py:55-65 — `dtype = _active_lora_dtype(hidden_states)` ... `hidden_states = hidden_states.to(dtype)` ... `return Opaque_LoRA_QKV.apply(...)` with no dtype guard. `grep -rn "_lora_projections_use_dtype\|_active_adapters_use_dtype" packages/` returns only _utils.py, mlp.py and linear.py.

RUN /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/qkvaudit/mixedprec.py (CPU, is_cuda forced, bf16 Llama + fp32 adapters, autocast OFF, LoRA on q/k/v/o): `base weight dtype: torch.bfloat16 | lora_A dtype: torch.float32`, `fused kernels actually invoked: ['Opaque_LoRA_QKV']` (Opaque_LoRA_W correctly declined), `max abs diff (bf16 logits): 0.00390625  ref scale: 0.54296875` vs the PEFT reference.

The tests added by 5b41925c for QKV (packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_fused_lora_qkv.py:58-121, :123-185) exercise only the *autocast-enabled* case (`with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)`), which is precisely the branch the guard skips; the no-autocast branch is untested for QKV.
findings.fix_sketch: Add to `_opaque_fused_lora_qkv` the same early-out used by linear.py/mlp.py: `if not torch.is_autocast_enabled("cuda") and not _lora_projections_use_dtype(self, ("q_proj","k_proj","v_proj"), dtype): return self.q_proj(h), self.k_proj(h), self.v_proj(h)` — but note the fallback has to run *inside* the wrapper, so it is cleaner to move the check into `_auto_fuse_lora`'s runtime path or have the wrapper delegate to `original_forward` when the dtypes disagree. Add a no-autocast bf16-model/fp32-adapter parity test for QKV.

findings.title: Fused QKV validates its preconditions only at patch time and reads only active_adapters[0], so adapter switching silently drops dropout and extra adapters
findings.claim: `_auto_fuse_lora` evaluates `_no_lora_dropout` and `_bias_is_frozen` once, when the wrapper is installed, and then never again. At runtime `_extract_lora_params` reads `lora_linear.active_adapters[0]` only. The sibling `Opaque_LoRA_W` path in linear.py re-derives `dropout_is_noop` on every forward and falls back to PEFT when it is not a no-op (linear.py:37-46), and explicitly folds in `self.active_adapters[1:]` (linear.py:75-82). The fused QKV path does neither, so (a) after `set_adapter()` to an adapter with `lora_dropout>0` the fused Q/K/V projections silently skip dropout while o_proj and the MLP still apply it, and (b) with several active adapters the fused Q/K/V silently apply only the first while o_proj applies all of them.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Patch a model whose 'clean' adapter has dropout 0, then `pm.add_adapter('noisy', LoraConfig(lora_dropout=0.9, ...)); pm.base_model.set_adapter('noisy'); pm.train()`. Q/K/V run deterministically with no regularization; the user believes dropout 0.9 is active. (b) Multi-adapter serving/training with `set_adapter(['a','b'])`: adapter b's contribution to Q/K/V is dropped entirely, and its q/k/v LoRA parameters receive zero gradient.
evidence: CURRENT TREE _router.py:78-97 — the gate block runs once inside `_auto_fuse_lora`, then `attn.forward = types.MethodType(fused_qkv_fwd, attn); attn._opaque_lora_qkv_patched = True`. components/_utils.py:50-58 — `if (lora_linear.disable_adapters or not lora_linear.active_adapters or lora_linear.active_adapters[0] not in lora_linear.lora_A): return W, None, None, 0.0` / `active = lora_linear.active_adapters[0]`.
Contrast components/linear.py:37-46 (`dropout_is_noop` recomputed per call, falls back to `original`) and linear.py:75-82 (`for adapter in self.active_adapters[1:]: ... result = result + lora_out`).

RUN /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/qkvaudit/dropoutswitch.py (CPU, is_cuda forced): after switching to an adapter with `Dropout(p=0.9)` in train mode — `stochastic spread across 4 fused forwards in train mode (should be >0 if dropout applied): 0.0` vs `spread with unfused PEFT forward: 0.768401`.

RUN /tmp/.../qkvaudit/multiadapter.py: `active adapters on q_proj: ['a', 'b']`, `fused: True`, `peft(a+b) vs fused: 0.8043` while `peft(a only) vs peft(a+b): 0.7743` — the fused Q/K/V behave as if adapter b were absent.

Gate behaviour at patch time is correct and was verified separately (/tmp/.../qkvaudit/gates.py): bias='all' -> fused=False, bias='lora_only' -> fused=False, lora_dropout=0.1 -> fused=False, partial target_modules -> fused=False.
findings.fix_sketch: In `_opaque_fused_lora_qkv`, re-check the preconditions per call and delegate to the unfused projections when they no longer hold: `if len(active_adapters) > 1 or dropout is not a no-op or any base bias requires grad: return self.q_proj(h), self.k_proj(h), self.v_proj(h)`. Alternatively mirror linear.py and add the extra-adapter deltas after the fused call. Tests: switch adapters after patching and assert the fused path either applies dropout/extra adapters or falls back.

findings.title: Fused QKV wrapper closes over a bound original_forward, so a deepcopy of a patched model routes the copy's fallback to the original model's attention
findings.claim: `fused_qkv_fwd = fused_forward_factory(attn.forward)` captures a *bound* method of that specific attention instance inside the wrapper's closure, and the wrapper is then installed as an instance attribute. `copy.deepcopy` rebinds the outer `types.MethodType` to the copy (via `_deepcopy_method`) but copies the wrapper function — and hence its closure cell holding the original bound `original_forward` — by reference. Every non-CUDA call on the copy (qkv.py:109-117, qkv_gemma3.py:110-117, qkv_qwen3.py:108-115) therefore executes the *original* model's attention, reading the original model's weights. On a CPU-only host the fallback is the only path, so a deepcopied model is entirely aliased through attention.
findings.failure_scenario: TR-DPO builds its reference model as `ref = ref_model if ref_model is not None else copy.deepcopy(model)` (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:729). On a CPU run (`args.device` == cpu, so `ref.to(self._precompute_device)` keeps it on CPU) the reference model's attention silently tracks the *policy* model's live LoRA weights, so the DPO reference logprobs move with the policy and the KL term collapses. The same aliasing hits any CPU evaluation copy or any EMA/averaged copy of a patched model.
evidence: CURRENT TREE _router.py:89-96 — `attn._opaque_fused_qkv = types.MethodType(_opaque_fused_lora_qkv, attn)` / `fused_qkv_fwd = fused_forward_factory(attn.forward)` / `attn.forward = types.MethodType(fused_qkv_fwd, attn)`. qkv.py:87-117 — the factory's `forward` closes over `original_forward` and calls it verbatim when `not hidden_states.is_cuda`.

RUN /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/qkvaudit/deepcopy.py (plain CPU, no is_cuda patch, so the fallback is live): `patched: True`, `clone forward __self__ is clone attn: True`, `captured original_forward bound to ORIGINAL attn?: [True]`, and after `attn.q_proj.lora_B['default'].weight.add_(5.0)` on the ORIGINAL model, `clone output changed after mutating ORIGINAL model: 0.6004`.

Reachable call site: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:729 `ref = ref_model if ref_model is not None else copy.deepcopy(model)`; :685 and :732 `ref.to(self._precompute_device).eval()`; :405 `self._precompute_device = args.device`.
`_opaque_fused_qkv` itself is safe because `_opaque_fused_lora_qkv` is a module-level function, so deepcopy rebinds `__self__` correctly — only the captured `original_forward` is stale.
findings.fix_sketch: Capture the *unbound* function and re-bind at call time: `original_forward = type(attn).forward` in `_auto_fuse_lora`, and have the wrappers call `original_forward(self, hidden_states, ...)`. Add a `__deepcopy__`-safe smoke test: deepcopy a patched model, perturb the original's adapters, assert the copy's CPU output is unchanged.

findings.title: No fused-vs-unfused parity test exists for the generic QKV wrapper on any device; the Gemma3 device-independent pipeline pattern was not reused for Qwen3 or the generic path
findings.line: 26-51 (only CPU test is routing/fallback); 54 (@pytest.mark.cuda gates everything numeric)
findings.claim: The four delta commits each shipped tests, but the parity coverage is family-shaped rather than wrapper-shaped. Gemma3 got a genuine device-independent pipeline suite (`TestGemma3FusedWrapperPipeline`, tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:143-234) that stubs `_opaque_fused_qkv` with the unfused projections and compares the wrapper against upstream `attn(...)` on CPU. Qwen3 got no equivalent — `_fused_qkv_qwen3_attention_forward` is referenced by no test at all (verified by grep), and its numeric tests are inside the `@pytest.mark.cuda` class. The generic wrapper `_make_fused_qkv_attention_forward`, which serves five of the eight eligible families (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Gemma2, Granite, Cohere2, Qwen2, GLM4), is referenced by no test whatsoever, and every CUDA parity test uses Qwen2/Qwen3/Gemma3/GLM4 — the families where the generic wrapper happens to be faithful. The two silent-corruption defects above are exactly what that shape of coverage cannot see. (Distinct from tracked #880, which is about restoring CUDA markers for existing LoRA kernel tests, and from #968, which proposes packing more projections.)
findings.failure_scenario: Any future change to the generic wrapper, or any new family added to `_FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES`, ships with no test that would notice a dropped attention argument, a wrong rotary placement, or a missing q_norm — the failure mode already realized for Cohere2, Mistral and Gemma2.
evidence: `grep -rn "_make_fused_qkv_attention_forward|_fused_qkv_qwen3_attention_forward" packages/` — no hits under packages/*/tests; only src and .pyc.

packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_fused_lora_qkv.py:26 `def test_qwen3_qkv_fusion_routes_and_falls_back_on_cpu()` asserts only `hasattr(attn, "_opaque_fused_qkv")` and `torch.isfinite(model(input_ids).logits).all()`; line 54 `@pytest.mark.cuda class TestFusedLoRAQKV` contains every numeric test.
packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_glm4_lora.py:21 `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(...)` + :43 `@pytest.mark.cuda` — the whole GLM4 file is CUDA-only.

packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:126-139 `_install_reference_fused_qkv` — the working pattern that would have caught the generic-wrapper defects if applied to Cohere2/Mistral/Gemma2.

The only Cohere2 fused test (test_fused_lora_parallel_residual.py) compares vmap vs eager of the *same fused* model and uses num_hidden_layers=1, so it is structurally unable to detect a wrapper-vs-upstream divergence.

Coverage of family routing itself was checked and is currently exact: a scan of all 478 importable `transformers.models.*.modeling_*` modules in transformers 5.15.1 found exactly the ten expected attention classes resolving through `_resolve_fused_qkv_forward_factory`; no look-alike family is mis-routed.
findings.fix_sketch: Parameterize the Gemma3 `_install_reference_fused_qkv` pipeline test over every entry in `_FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES` plus the two dedicated sets, building each family's tiny config with a sliding-window/softcap/NoPE-bearing layer count (>= 4 layers for Cohere2, seq_len > sliding_window for Mistral/Gemma2) and asserting `allclose(wrapper_out, attn(...))` on CPU. That is device-independent, cheap, and would have failed on all three defects.

findings.title: _auto_fuse_lora skips MLP fusion for any layer whose attention is already QKV-patched
findings.claim: The idempotency guard `if getattr(attn, "_opaque_lora_qkv_patched", False): continue` continues the *outer per-layer loop*, not just the QKV block, so on any second call to `apply_peft_model_patches` the MLP-fusion half of the loop body (lines 99-137) never runs for that layer. A layer whose MLP became eligible only after the first call therefore never gets fused.
findings.failure_scenario: `apply_model_patches(model)` runs during DPTrainer construction and fuses QKV (MLP not eligible yet, e.g. adapters added to gate/up/down afterwards); a later `apply_peft_model_patches(model)` short-circuits on the QKV flag and silently leaves every MLP unfused. Performance-only — results stay correct — but the intended optimization is silently absent with no log line.
evidence: CURRENT TREE packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/_router.py:68-72 — `attn = getattr(layer, "self_attn", None)` / `if attn is not None:` / `    if getattr(attn, "_opaque_lora_qkv_patched", False):` / `        continue`; the MLP block begins at line 99 inside the same `for layer in layers:` body.
`git log -L 60,75:.../peft/_router.py` shows the `continue` predates and survives both 41722a0b (#947) and 8ced13cf (#951), which rewrote the surrounding gate.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace `continue` with a guarded block, e.g. `if attn is not None and not getattr(attn, "_opaque_lora_qkv_patched", False): <qkv fusion>` so control falls through to the MLP section.

clean_areas: Fused-vs-unfused numerical parity of the whole model, measured by running each family end to end on CPU with torch.Tensor.is_cuda monkeypatched True to force the fused branch (scripts under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/qkvaudit/): Llama, Gemma, Granite, GLM4, Qwen2 and Qwen3 are BIT-EXACT (max |diff| == 0.0) against unpatched upstream under both attn_implementation='eager' and 'sdpa'. Gemma3 is likewise bit-exact. Only Mistral, Gemma2 and Cohere2 diverge (reported above).

Qwen3 dedicated wrapper (qkv_qwen3.py, commit bf2190b9 #950) checked line-by-line against transformers 5.15.1 modeling_qwen3.py:246-276: q_norm/k_norm applied to the (*, heads, head_dim) view BEFORE transpose exactly as upstream, RoPE order, dropout ternary, scaling, sliding_window forwarded (qkv_qwen3.py:81), and the get_interface dispatch match. Verified numerically with use_sliding_window=True / max_window_layers=0 (layer_types all 'sliding_attention'): pure-vs-fused 0.0 under eager and sdpa.

Gemma3 dedicated wrapper (qkv_gemma3.py, commit 8ced13cf #951) checked against modeling_gemma3.py: q_norm/k_norm applied AFTER transpose (upstream does the same; equivalent for last-dim RMSNorm either way), sliding_window forwarded (qkv_gemma3.py:83). Whole-model parity 0.0 under eager and sdpa with sliding layers.

Per-sample DP gradient parity through torch.func.vmap(grad(...)) with torch.func.functional_call: compared every LoRA A/B gradient tensor fused-vs-unfused for llama, qwen2, qwen3, gemma3 and glm4 (script grads.py). Worst relative deviation 4.2e-07 in fp32 — consistent with addmm_ reassociation, not a semantic difference. This also confirms Opaque_LoRA_QKV.setup_context correctly detects needs_weight_grads under functorch grad tracking (a False there would have produced zero adapter gradients).

GQA grouping and head counts in the fused path: all parity runs used num_attention_heads=4 / num_key_value_heads=2 (n_rep=2) with an explicit head_dim, exercising Q.view(hidden_shape) for the wide Q and the narrow K/V. No head-count constant is hard-coded in qkv.py / qkv_qwen3.py / qkv_gemma3.py; hidden_shape is derived from self.head_dim in all three.

Bias handling introduced by 41722a0b (#947): Opaque_LoRA_QKV.forward (kernels/lora.py:509-530) uses F.linear(X, W, b) for each projection and _require_frozen_qkv_biases (lora.py:96-105) raises ConfigurationError if any base bias requires grad, in both the eager and vmap rules. Verified numerically that the biased families (Qwen2 attention_bias=True, GLM4 attention_bias=True) are bit-exact fused-vs-unfused.

Fusion eligibility gates, exercised on CPU (gates.py): LoraConfig(bias='all') -> not fused; bias='lora_only' -> not fused (PEFT marks the base bias trainable through BaseTunerLayer.__getattr__); lora_dropout=0.1 -> not fused; LoRA on only q/k (partial coverage) -> not fused. _bias_is_frozen and _no_lora_dropout therefore fail safe at patch time (the runtime re-check gap is reported separately).

Behaviour for families NOT in the eligibility sets: _resolve_fused_qkv_forward_factory returns None and _auto_fuse_lora simply skips QKV fusion (no exception, no fallback to a wrong wrapper); per-projection Opaque_LoRA_W still applies via the patched peft.Linear.forward. Confirmed by resolving the factory for Ministral, Cohere, Olmo2, Olmo3, Phi3, SmolLM3, Exaone4, DeepseekV4, Qwen3Moe, Qwen3Next, Qwen3_5Moe, Mixtral, GptOss, HunYuanMoEV1 and Mellum attention classes -> all None. Silent loss of an optimization, never a correctness risk.

Class-name-through-MRO routing is currently unambiguous: scanned all 478 importable transformers.models.*.modeling_* modules in transformers 5.15.1 and found exactly ten attention classes that resolve through _resolve_fused_qkv_forward_factory (the eight generic + Gemma3 + Qwen3). No unrelated family inherits or reuses one of the matched class names, so there is no look-alike mis-fusion today.

KV-cache call shape: both the generic and the dedicated wrappers call past_key_values.update(k, v, self.layer_idx, cache_kwargs); transformers 5.15.1 Cache.update / DynamicCache.update are (self, key_states, value_states, layer_idx, *args, **kwargs), so the extra positional cache_kwargs is absorbed. Gemma3's cached-decoding parity test (test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:185-214) exercises this on CPU and passes.

Opaque_LoRA_QKV backward math derived and checked by hand against the forward Q = X Wq^T + bq + s_q (X Aq) Bq: _lora_qkv_backward_lite (kernels/lora.py:389-414) computes dX = sum_p grad_p W_p + s_p (grad_p B_p^T) A_p^T, and _lora_qkv_weight_backward_impl (lora.py:293-318) computes dA = s X^T (grad B^T), dB = s (A^T X^T) grad — both correct for the stored layouts (A is (in, rank), B is (rank, out)). Adapter gradients are computed from the ORIGINAL (uncast) saved A/B and X because setup_context receives pre-cast inputs, so they retain fp32 precision even when the forward ran in bf16.

The three delta commits' claim that Gemma3/Qwen3 'normalize Q/K after projection' and therefore need dedicated wrappers was verified against upstream: no other family in _FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES has q_norm/k_norm (checked Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Gemma2, Granite, Cohere2, Qwen2, Glm4 attention __init__ in transformers 5.15.1), so the generic wrapper's omission of q_norm is correct for the families it serves.

Did NOT re-report: issue #968 (pack LoRA QKV/MLP into fewer GEMMs), #880 (restore CUDA marker coverage for LoRA kernel tests), #898 (repeated-backward gap in remaining fused kernels) — all tracked. Opaque_LoRA_QKV.backward does call ctx.maybe_clear_saved_tensors() and del X, which is the #898 pattern; left to that issue.
